PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Uncultured placental material
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referring Institution: [redacted location]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetus with abnormalities on prenatal evaluation

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy screening

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured placental material to detect aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y. Multiple polymorphic microsatellite markers were amplified for each chromosome using fluorescently labeled primers. PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak areas were calculated and dosage ratios determined for informative markers. A minimum of two informative markers per chromosome were required for reliable interpretation.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D13S631: 1:1 ratio
- D13S258: 1:1 ratio
- D13S742: 1:1 ratio

Chromosome 15: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D15S659: 1:1 ratio
- D15S122: 1:1 ratio

Chromosome 16: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D16S539: 1:1 ratio
- D16S3018: 1:1 ratio

Chromosome 18: TRISOMY DETECTED
- D18S391: 2:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D18S390: 2:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D18S535: 1:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D18S386: 2:1 diallelic pattern (dosage ratio 2.1)
- D18S858: 2:1 diallelic pattern (dosage ratio 2.0)
- D18S978: 2:1 diallelic pattern (dosage ratio 2.1)
- D18S1002: 1:1:1 triallelic pattern
- D18S819: 2:1 diallelic pattern (dosage ratio 2.0)
- D18S51: 2:1 diallelic pattern (dosage ratio 2.1)

Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D21S1411: 1:1 ratio
- D21S1435: 1:1 ratio
- D21S1270: 1:1 ratio

Chromosome 22: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D22S1045: 1:1 ratio
- PENTA D: 1:1 ratio

Sex Chromosomes: Female (XX)
- AMELX/Y: Single X peak detected
- X22: Two alleles detected, normal female pattern
- DXYS218: Single X allele detected

Triploidy Assessment: EXCLUDED
- All informative autosomal markers show either 1:1 or 2:1 ratios
- No 2:1:1 patterns observed on multiple chromosomes

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis demonstrates trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome) in the fetal sample. Nine informative markers on chromosome 18 show either triallelic patterns or abnormal dosage ratios consistent with three copies of chromosome 18. All other tested chromosomes (13, 15, 16, 21, 22) show normal biparental inheritance patterns. The sex chromosome complement is female (XX). Triploidy has been excluded based on the marker patterns.

Trisomy 18 is associated with severe developmental abnormalities and is likely causative for the fetal abnormalities observed on prenatal evaluation. The majority of trisomy 18 cases arise as de novo events due to maternal meiotic nondisjunction, with risk increasing with maternal age. While this appears to be a sporadic aneuploidy, QF-PCR cannot fully exclude a parental chromosome rearrangement predisposing to trisomy 18.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is strongly advised to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
2. Parental karyotyping is available if desired for reassurance regarding balanced rearrangements
3. There is a slightly increased risk for trisomy 18 in future pregnancies (approximately 1% above age-related risk)
4. For future pregnancies, recommend:
   - First trimester combined screening or cell-free DNA screening
   - Detailed ultrasound monitoring
   - Prenatal diagnosis (CVS or amniocentesis) is available
5. Consider referral to maternal-fetal medicine for pregnancy management options

This test was developed and validated by the [redacted location] Cytogenetics Laboratory. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other laboratory data.

Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
